en: An overseer of congregations: either any such overseer, generally speaking, or (in Eastern Orthodoxy, Catholicism, Anglicanism, etc.) an …
A chief of the Festival of Fools or St. Nicholas Day.
To act as a bishop, to perform the duties of a bishop, especially to confirm another's membership in the church.
To make a bishop.

bishop.ety:
From Middle English bischop, bishop, bisshop, biscop, from Old English bisċop (“bishop”), from Proto-West Germanic *biskop, from Vulgar Latin (e)biscopus, from classical Latin episcopus (“overseer, supervisor”), from Ancient Greek ἐπίσκοπος (epískopos, “overseer”), from ἐπί (epí, “over”) + σκοπός (skopós, “watcher”), used in Greek and Latin both generally and as a title of civil officers. Cognate with all European terms for the position in various Christian churches; compare also Middle English bisp (“bishop”).
* The Tyndale Bible uses native English overseer instead.

ex.en: The bishops were in favor of the proposition.
ex.ja: 司教達はその提案に賛成であった。

ex.en: The bishop took pity on the desperate immigrants.
ex.ja: 宗教は、自暴自棄になった移民達を哀れんで助けを与えた。

ex.en: The bishop felt pity for the immigrants who were abandoned, and gave them help.
ex.ja: 司教は、自暴自棄になった移民たちを哀れんで助けを与えた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 episkopos（監督者）＝ epi（上から）+ skopein（見る）。「司教」→ チェスの「ビショップ」。scope と同じ。

en: As a rule; frequently; usually.

commonly.ety: Inherited from Middle English comunly; equivalent to common + -ly.

ex.en: Women commonly live longer than men.
ex.ja: 女性は通常男性よりも長生きする。

ex.en: This sentence is commonly used.
ex.ja: この文はよく使われるよ。

ex.en: Antibiotics are commonly enzymatic inhibitors.
ex.ja: 抗生物質は一般的に酵素の阻害剤である。

note.ja: common（共通の・ふつうの）+ -ly。「一般に」。

en: Intended for defence; protective.
Intended to deter attack.
A means, attitude or position of defense. Chiefly in on the defensive.

defensive.ety: From Middle French défensif. Morphologically defense + -ive.

ex.en: Defensive driving can help you avoid accidents.
ex.ja: 予防運転は事故を防ぎます。

note.ja: defense（防御）+ -ive。de + fendere（打つ）。「防御の」。defend と同じ。

en: The extent to which a resource is used for the intended purpose.
The ratio of useful work to energy expended. Often given the symbol η.

efficiency.ety: From Latin efficientia, equivalent to efficient + -cy.

ex.en: He put forward a plan for improving office efficiency.
ex.ja: 彼は事務効率をよくする案を出した。

ex.en: That makes for efficiency.
ex.ja: そうすれば能率が上がりますよ。

ex.en: Efficiency is the dominant idea in business.
ex.ja: 商売では能率のよさということが最も重要な考えである。

note.ja: efficient（効率的な）+ -cy。ex + facere（作る）。「成果を作り出す」→「効率」。effect と同じ。

en: A company, business, organization, or other purposeful endeavor.
An undertaking, venture, or project, especially a daring and courageous one.
To undertake an enterprise, or something hazardous or difficult.
To undertake; to begin and attempt to perform; to venture upon.

enterprise.ety: From Old French via Middle English and Middle French entreprise, feminine past participle of entreprendre (“to undertake”), from entre (“in between”) + prendre (“to take”), from Latin inter + prehendō, see prehensile.

ex.en: Building the steel factory was a great enterprise.
ex.ja: その製鉄工場を建てるのは非常に大変な事業だった。

ex.en: He played an important part in the enterprise.
ex.ja: 彼はその事業において重要な役割を演じた。

ex.en: Your success in the enterprise depends on your effort.
ex.ja: その事業に成功するかどうかは君の努力しだいだ。

note.ja: enter（= inter 間に）+ pris（取る）+ e。手中に取ること →（困難なことに着手する）→「企業・事業・冒険心」。

en: A test under controlled conditions made to either demonstrate a known truth, examine the validity of a hypothesis, or determine the effic…
To conduct an experiment.
To try something to observe the results.

experiment.ety: From Middle English experiment, from Old French esperiment (French expérience), from Latin experimentum (“experience, attempt, experiment”), from experior (“to experience, to attempt”), itself from ex + *perior, in turn from Proto-Indo-European *per-.

ex.en: We used the following procedures in this experiment.
ex.ja: この実験には以下の手段を使用した。

ex.en: They carried out a new experiment in chemistry.
ex.ja: 彼らは化学の新しい実験をした。

ex.en: They conducted the following experiment to collect the data.
ex.ja: データを収集するため、次の実験を行った。

note.ja: ラテン語 experimentum（試み）から。experiri（試す）。experience と同じ語源。expert も同系。

en: A place for discussion.
A gathering for the purpose of discussion; a symposium.

forum.ety: From Latin forum (“public market place, forum”). Doublet of fuero and door.

ex.en: I moved the forum to a new server.
ex.ja: 掲示板を新しいサーバーに移転しました。

ex.en: The forum was moved to a new server.
ex.ja: 掲示板を新しいサーバーに移転しました。

ex.en: I do not have an account in these forums.
ex.ja: これらのフォームのアカウントを私はもってません。

note.ja: ラテン語 forum（広場）から。古代ローマの公共広場で議論が行われたことから「討論の場」。

en: Any plant of the family Poaceae, characterized by leaves that arise from nodes in the stem and leaf bases that wrap around the stem, espe…
Any of the various plants that are not in the family Poaceae that resemble grasses.
To lay out on the grass; to knock down (an opponent etc.).
To cover with grass or with turf.

grass.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *gʰreh₁-der.
Proto-Germanic *grasą
Proto-West Germanic *gras
Old English græs
Middle English gras
English grass
Inherited from Middle English gras, from Old English græs, from Proto-West Germanic *gras, from Proto-Germanic *grasą (“grass”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰreh₁- (“to grow”).
Cognates
Cognate with Scots gress (“grass”), North Frisian gaars, geers, Gērs, gjars, gjas, gäärs (“grass”), Saterland Frisian Gäärs (“grass”), West Frisian gers (“grass”), Cimbrian gras, grass (“grass”), German and Luxembourgish Gras (“grass, weed”), Dutch gras (“grass, turf,

ex.en: We laid the injured man on the grass.
ex.ja: 我々は傷ついた人を草の上に横たえた。

ex.en: This grass is too wet to sit on.
ex.ja: この芝生は座れないほどぬれている。

ex.en: The dog lying on the grass is mine.
ex.ja: 芝生に横になっている犬は、私の犬です。

note.ja: 古英語 græs から。grow（育つ）、green と同じ語根。

en: In the future from now.
As a result; therefore, for this reason.

hence.ety:
A later Middle English spelling, retaining the voiceless -s, of hennes (henne + adverbial genitive ending -s), from Old English heonan (“away", "hence”), from a Proto-West Germanic *hin-, from Proto-Germanic *hiz, and Proto-Germanic *-anē.
Cognate with Old Saxon hinan, Old High German hinnan (German hinnen), Dutch heen, Swedish hän. Related to Old English her (“here”).

ex.en: Hence, I shall have to stay here.
ex.ja: それゆえここにとどまらざるを得ないだろう。

ex.en: What will become of the world thirty years hence?
ex.ja: 今から３０年後に世界はどうなるだろう？

ex.en: Hence 50 percent of the muscle can give way to fat.
ex.ja: ゆえに、筋肉の５０パーセントが脂肪に取って代わられる可能性がある。

note.ja: 古英語 heonan（ここから）+ -s。here と同系。「ここから」→「今から」→「それゆえ」。

en: Increasing in amount or intensity.

increasingly.ety: From Middle English encreessingli, equivalent to increasing + -ly.

ex.en: Modern finance is becoming increasingly complicated and sophisticated.
ex.ja: 現代の金融は一段と複雑かつ高度になってきている。

ex.en: In recent years electronic computers have become increasingly important.
ex.ja: 近年では、電子コンピューターがますます重要になってきた。

ex.en: The world's aviation industry is growing increasingly worried about crashes.
ex.ja: 世界の航空産業は墜落事故についての懸念を募らせている。

note.ja: increasing（増えている）+ -ly。in + crescere（成長する）。「ますます」。increase と同じ cresc。

en: In an incredible manner; not to be believed.
To a great extent; extremely.

incredibly.ety:
Etymology tree
English incredible
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English incredibly
From incredible + -ly.

ex.en: Tom is incredibly bad at drawing.
ex.ja: トムはびっくりするくらいに絵が下手だ。

ex.en: This summer is incredibly hot.
ex.ja: 今年の夏は異常に暑い。

ex.en: George has an incredibly large Adam's apple.
ex.ja: ジョージののどぼとけは信じられないぐらい大きい。

note.ja: incredible（信じられない）+ -ly。in + credibilis（信じられる）。credit と同じ cred。

zh: 新聞工作者 /新闻工作者

en: The keeper of a personal journal, who writes in it regularly.
One whose occupation is journalism, originally only writing in the printed press.

journalist.ety:
Etymology tree
English journal
Proto-Indo-European *-id-
Proto-Indo-European *-yéti
Proto-Indo-European *-idyéti

Ancient Greek -ῐστής (-ĭstḗs)bor.
Latin -istader.
Old French -istebor.
Middle English -ist
English -ist
English journalist
From journal + -ist.

ex.en: The journalist was calm even in an emergency.
ex.ja: その記者は緊急事態のときでも落ち着いていた。

ex.en: I thought of the woman as a journalist.
ex.ja: 私はその女性を記者だと思っていた。

ex.en: I've made up my mind to become a journalist.
ex.ja: 私はジャーナリストになる決心をしました。

note.ja: journal（新聞・日誌）+ -ist。「記者」。

en: A grinding apparatus for substances such as grains, seeds, etc. (Some are small and simple, and some are large and complex.)
The building housing such a grinding apparatus; also, any similar building that houses a similarly material activity (such as weaving, fu…
To grind or otherwise process in a mill or other machine.
To shape, polish, dress or finish using a machine.

mill.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *melh₂-
Proto-Indo-European *-ti
Proto-Indo-European *mélh₂ti

Latin molō

English mill
From Middle English mylne, mille, from Old English mylen, from Proto-West Germanic *mulīnu (“mill”), from Late Latin molīna, molīnum, molīnus (“mill”), from Latin molō (“grind, mill”, verb), closely allied to Proto-Germanic *muljaną (“to crush, grind”) (see English mills

ex.en: There is a water mill above the bridge.
ex.ja: この橋の上流に水車小屋がある。

ex.en: The coffee mill that I received does not work.
ex.ja: 受け取ったコーヒーミルが動きません。

ex.en: There was a water mill below the dam.
ex.ja: ダムの下流に水車小屋があった。

note.ja: ラテン語 mola（ひき臼）から古英語に入った語。「製粉所」→「工場」。meal（ひき割り粉）、molar（臼歯）と同系。

en: A favorable opportunity; a convenient or timely chance.
The time when something happens.
To cause; to produce; to induce

occasion.ety: From Middle English occasioun, from Middle French occasion, from Old French occasiun, from Latin occāsiōnem, noun of action from perfect passive participle occāsus, from verb occidō, from prefix ob- (“down", "away”) + verb cadō (“fall”).

ex.en: I meet him on occasion at the club.
ex.ja: 時折クラブで彼に会います。

ex.en: He offered his congratulations on the happy occasion.
ex.ja: そのめでたいときに当たり彼は祝辞を述べた。

ex.en: I never have had occasion to use it.
ex.ja: 今までそれを使う機会がなかった。

note.ja: oc（〜に向かって）+ cas（落ちる）+ ion。降りかかってくる時 →「場合・機会・行事」。

ja: ゆっくり行ったり来たりする

en: A step taken with the foot.
The distance covered in a step (or sometimes two), either vaguely or according to various specific set measurements.
Describing a bowler who bowls fast balls.
To walk back and forth in a small distance.
To walk along or through sth with regular strides.
With all due respect to.

pace.ety: From Middle English pase, from Anglo-Norman pas, Old French pas, and their source, Latin passus. Doublet of pas and fathom; compare also pass. Cognate with pass, Spanish pasear, paso.

ex.en: I want to go at my own pace.
ex.ja: マイペースに生きたい。

ex.en: I want to live at my own pace.
ex.ja: マイペースに生きたい。

ex.en: I want to work at my own pace.
ex.ja: マイペースで仕事したい。

note.ja: ラテン語 passus（歩み）から。pandere（広げる：足を広げる）。「一歩」→「速さ」。pass と同系。

en: One who rides or travels in a vehicle, but who does not operate it and is not a member of the crew.
Somebody in a team who does not do their fair share of the work.
To ride as a passenger in a vehicle.

passenger.ety: From Old French passagier with intrusive n (see etymology of messenger).

ex.en: Why didn't they draw up a passenger list?
ex.ja: 彼らはなぜ乗客名簿を作らなかったのだろう。

ex.en: The bag I left on the passenger seat is missing!
ex.ja: 助手席に置いていた鞄がない！

ex.en: There are very few passengers in the train.
ex.ja: その列車の乗客はほんの僅かしかいない。

note.ja: passage（通行）+ -er。n は後から加わった（messenger と同じ）。「通る人」→「乗客」。

en: An enclosure (enclosed area) used to contain domesticated animals, especially sheep or cattle.
The bullpen.
To enclose in a pen.

pen.ety:
From Middle English pen, penne (“enclosure for animals”), from Old English penn (“enclosure, fold, pen”), from Proto-Germanic *pennō, *pannijō (“pin, bolt, nail, tack”), from Proto-Indo-European *bend- (“pointed peg, nail, edge”). Related to pin.
Sense “prison” originally figurative extension to “enclosure for persons” (1845), later influenced by penitentiary (“prison”), being analyzed as an abbreviation (1884).

ex.en: This is the pen that I lost yesterday.
ex.ja: これは、私が昨日なくしたペンです。

ex.en: Which is longer, this pen or that one?
ex.ja: このペンとあのペンではどちらが長いですか。

ex.en: That pen is more expensive than this one.
ex.ja: あのペンはこのペンよりも高価だ。

note.ja: 「ペン」はラテン語 penna（羽）から。羽ペンを使ったことから。「囲い」は古英語 penn からで別語。

en: An honorary title of the Roman Catholic bishop of Rome as father and head of his church, a sovereign of the Vatican city state.
Any similarly absolute and 'infallible' authority.
To act as or like a pope.
To convert to Roman Catholicism.

pope.ety: From Middle English pope, popa, from Old English pāpa, from Vulgar Latin papa (title for priests and bishops, esp. and by 8th c. only the bishop of Rome), from early Medieval Greek παπᾶς (papâs, title for priests and bishops, especially by 3rd c. the bishop of Alexandria), from late Ancient Greek πάπας (pápas, title for priests and bishops, in the sense of spiritual father), from πάππας (páppas, “papa, daddy”).

ex.en: We have a Pope.
ex.ja: われらは教皇を得た。

ex.en: The pope appeared in his red robe.
ex.ja: 法王は赤い法衣をまとって現れた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 pappas（父）から。「ローマ教皇」。papa と同じ。

en: A control or occupancy of something for which one does not necessarily have private property rights.
Something that is owned.

possession.ety: From Latin possessiō, possessiōnis. Equivalent to possess + -ion.

ex.en: I have never had more than $500 in my possession.
ex.ja: 私は５００ドル以上を持ち歩いたことがありません。

ex.en: He is in possession of this land.
ex.ja: 彼はこの土地を所有している。

ex.en: All his possessions are contained in that box.
ex.ja: 彼の所持品は全部あの箱に入っている。

note.ja: possess（所有する）+ -ion。ラテン語 possidere ＝ potis（力のある）+ sedere（座る）。「主として座っている」→「所有」。

en: Very swift or quick.
Steep, changing altitude quickly. (of a slope)
A rough section of a river or stream which is difficult to navigate due to the swift and turbulent motion of the water.

rapid.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₁reh₁p-
Proto-Indo-European *-yéti
Proto-Indo-European *h₁r̥h₁pyéti
Proto-Italic *rapjō
Latin rapiō
Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁-der.
Proto-Italic *-iðos
Latin -idus
Latin rapidusder.
Middle French rapidebor.
▲
Latin rapidusbor.
English rapid
Borrowed from Middle French rapide and its etymon Latin rapidus.

ex.en: There was a rapid decline in stock prices.
ex.ja: 株価の急激な下落があった。

ex.en: Science has made rapid progress in this century.
ex.ja: 科学は今世紀になって急速な進歩を遂げた。

ex.en: The rapid growth of the city surprised us.
ex.ja: その都市の急速な発展に私たちは驚いた。

note.ja: ラテン語 rapidus（奪い去る・急な）から。rapere（奪う）。「急速な」。rape、rapture と同じ。

en: The ordinal form of the number six.
The person or thing in the sixth position.
One of six equal parts of a whole.

sixth.ety: From earlier sixt, from Middle English sixte, from Old English siexta, from Proto-Germanic *sehstô. By surface analysis, six + -th (ordinal suffix).

ex.en: June is the sixth month of the year.
ex.ja: 「６月」は１年の中で６回目の月にあたります。

ex.en: She knew it by a sixth sense.
ex.ja: 彼女は第六感でそれが分かった。

ex.en: The office has been transferred up to the sixth floor.
ex.ja: 事務所は６階に移った。

note.ja: six の序数。

en: To rotate, revolve, gyrate (usually quickly); to partially or completely rotate to face another direction.
To enter, or remain in, a spin (abnormal stalled flight mode).
Circular motion, usually rapid.
A state of confusion or disorientation.

spin.ety:
From Middle English spinnen, from Old English spinnan, from Proto-Germanic *spinnaną, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)penh₁-.
Cognates
Cognate with Dutch, German spinnen (“to spin”), Luxembourgish spannen (“to spin”), Yiddish שפּינען (shpinen, “spin”), Danish spinde (“to spin”), Faroese, Icelandic and Swedish spinna (“to spin”), Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk spinne (“to spin”), Gothic 𐍃𐍀𐌹𐌽𐌽𐌰𐌽 (spinnan, “to spin”).

ex.en: I'm so busy it makes my head spin.
ex.ja: 目が回るほど忙しいよ。

ex.en: After dinner, we took a spin around town in my car.
ex.ja: 食後、私の車で町を一走りした。

ex.en: My head is spinning because of the heat.
ex.ja: 暑さで頭が回らない。

note.ja: 古英語 spinnan から。「糸を紡ぐ」→「回転する」→ 話を都合よく「ひねる」。spider（糸を紡ぐもの）と同じ。

en: Having sufficient or the required properties for a certain purpose or task; appropriate to a certain occasion.

suitable.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *sekʷ-
Proto-Indo-European *sékʷetor
Proto-Italic *sekʷōr
Vulgar Latin sequor, sequi
Vulgar Latin *sequere
Vulgar Latin *sequita
Old French siute
Anglo-Norman suitebor.
Middle English sute
English suit
Proto-Indo-European *-dʰlom
Proto-Italic *-ðlom
Proto-Italic *-ðlis
Latin -bilis
Latin -ābilis
Old French -ablebor.
Middle English -able
English -able
English suitable
From suit + -able.

ex.en: The job is not suitable for young girls.
ex.ja: その仕事は若い女性には適当ではない。

ex.en: This material is not suitable for a dress.
ex.ja: この生地は洋服をつくるのには向かない。

ex.en: He is far from suitable for that job.
ex.ja: 彼はあの仕事にはまったく不向きな人です。

note.ja: suit（似合う・適する）+ able。→「適した・ふさわしい」。

en: The cardinal number occurring after twenty-nine and before thirty-one, represented in Arabic numerals as 30.
A commercial lasting 30 seconds.

thirty.ety: From Middle English thirty, metathetic alternant of thritty, from Old English þrītiġ, þrittiġ (“thirty”), from Proto-Germanic *þrīz tigiwiz (“thirty”, literally “three tens”), equivalent to three + -ty. Cognate with Scots therty, tretty (“thirty”), West Frisian tritich (“thirty”), Dutch dertig (“thirty”), German dreißig (“thirty”).

ex.en: There were thirty people present at the meeting.
ex.ja: その会議に出席していたのは３０名の人であった。

ex.en: The bus is capable of carrying thirty people.
ex.ja: このバスは３０人を運ぶことができる。

ex.en: I got up at six-thirty this morning.
ex.ja: けさは６時半に起きた。

note.ja: three + -ty（10）。「3つの10」。

en: Well-grounded or justifiable, pertinent.
Acceptable, proper or correct; in accordance with the rules.

valid.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₂welh₁-
Proto-Indo-European *-éh₁ti

Proto-Indo-European *-éh₁yeti

Latin validusder.
Middle French validebor.
English valid
Borrowed from Middle French valide (“healthy, sound, in good order”), from Latin validus, from valeō (“to be strong, to be healthy, to be worth”) + -idus, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂welh₁- (“be strong”).

ex.en: The ticket is valid for a week.
ex.ja: その切符は一週間有効です。

ex.en: This is a valid point of view.
ex.ja: これは十分根拠のある視点だ。

ex.en: This ticket is valid for three months.
ex.ja: この列車乗車券は３カ月有効だ。

note.ja: val（強い・価値がある）+ id。効力が強い →「有効な・妥当な」。

en: Relating to or characteristic of life.
Necessary to the continuation of life; being the seat of life; being that on which life depends.

vital.ety: From Middle English vital, from Old French vital, from Latin vītālis (“of life, life-giving”), from vīta (“life”), from vīvō (“to live”). Doublet of jiva and quick.

ex.en: Water is a natural resource of vital importance.
ex.ja: 水は極めて重要な天然資源の１つだ。

ex.en: Public opinion plays a vital role in politics.
ex.ja: 世論は政治の領域で重要な役割を演ずる。

ex.en: There's a vital link between the two.
ex.ja: ２つの間には重要なつながりがある。

note.ja: ラテン語 vita（命）から。vit + al。命にかかわる →「不可欠な・生き生きした」。vitamin（命のアミン）も同じ。

en: Often preceded by the: During the time; meanwhile.

whilst.ety: From Late Middle English whilst, whilest, qwhilste (Northern England), quilest (Northwest Midlands) [and other forms], from whiles (“during the time that, while; only so long as; provided that; because, since; until”) + -t (excrescent suffix, perhaps due to a combination of -(e)s and the following word the, or influenced by the superlative suffix -est). Whiles is derived from whiles (“period of time, a while”, noun) (probably from the second element of adverbs and conjunctions like otherwhiles and somewhiles), from while (“period of time, a while”, noun) + -s (suffix forming adverbs of manner,

ex.en: I will introduce it whilst showing you photos.

ex.ja: 混浴を楽しみながら会話に花をさかせました。

ex.en: Whilst on my way to school, I happened to catch sight of my uncle.
ex.ja: 学校に行く途中で、叔父さんを見掛けたんだ。

note.ja: while の古い形に -st がついた語。主にイギリスで使う。amongst と同じ作り。

ex.ja: 彼は農業大学へ行きました。

ex.ja: バイオテクノロジーは農業に革命をもたらすだろう。

en: To adduce (something) as a reason, excuse, support etc.
To make a claim as justification or proof; to make an assertion without proof.

allege.ety: From Middle English aleggen, perhaps from Old French alleguer, or from Anglo-Norman aleger, the form perhaps from Old French esligier (“to acquit”), from Medieval Latin *exlītigāre (“to clear at law”), from Latin ex (“out”) + lītigō (“sue at law”), but the meaning from Old French alleguer, from Latin allēgāre (“send on a mission, depute; relate, mention, adduce”), from ad (“to”) + lēgō (“send”). ex.ja: その男がその殺人を犯したと言われている。

ex.ja: その新聞は彼の犯罪への掛かり合いを主張した。

ex.en: He is alleged to have poisoned his wife.
ex.ja: 彼は妻を毒殺したと言われている。

note.ja: 古フランス語 esligier（訴訟を起こす）から。ラテン語 allegare（申し立てる）と混同された。「申し立てる」。

en: The exchange or buying and selling of commodities; especially the exchange of merchandise, on a large scale, between different places or …
Social intercourse; the dealings of one person or class in society with another; familiarity.

commerce.ety: Borrowed from Middle French commerce, from Latin commercium. Doublet of comess. Displaced native Old English mangung.

ex.en: Commerce led to the development of cities.
ex.ja: 商業は都市の発展をもたらした。

ex.en: English is useful in commerce.
ex.ja: 英語は商業において役立つ。

ex.en: Osaka is the center of commerce in Japan.
ex.ja: 大阪は日本の商業の中心地です。

note.ja: ラテン語 commercium ＝ com（共に）+ merx（商品）。「商品のやりとり」→「商業」。merchant、market と同じ merc。

en: A small inlet, often saltwater, leading to the sea or to the main channel of a river, especially a river estuary.
The inner part of a port that is used as a dock for small boats.

creek.ety:

See also Old Dutch creka, crika (“inlet, cove, creek”), Medieval Latin creca, crica, kríkr (“angle, corner, nook, bay”), Old Norse kraki (“pole with a hook, anchor”), and possibly Old Norse krókr (“hook, bend, bight”). Mode

ex.en: The children caught small fish in the creek.
ex.ja: 子どもたちは小川で小さな魚を捕まえた。

note.ja: 古北欧語 kriki（隅・入り江）から。（英）入り江、（米）小川。

en: Money or other items used to facilitate transactions.
Paper money.

ex.ja: 外貨の為替レートは毎日変わる。

ex.ja: その習慣は日本ではほとんど行われていない。

ex.en: Currency and bond markets are relatively calm.
ex.ja: 通貨市場、債券市場は比較的落ち着いている。

note.ja: cur（走る・流れる）+ ren + cy。（手から手へ）流通しているもの →「通貨・流通」。current（流れ・現在の）も同じ。

en: A person's internal state of being and involuntary physiological response to an object or a situation, based on or tied to physical state…
A reaction by a non-human organism with behavioral and physiological elements similar to a person's response.

ex.en: His speech had an effect on our emotions.
ex.ja: 彼の演説は私達の感情に影響を与えた。

ex.en: Don't let your emotions rule you. Be calm!
ex.ja: 感情にはしるな。冷静になれ！

ex.en: Sometimes I can't help showing emotions.
ex.ja: 時々感情が抑えられないことがある。

note.ja: e（外へ）+ mot（動く）+ ion。心が外へ動き出すこと →「感情」。

en: An instance of exhibiting, or something exhibited.
A large-scale public showing of objects or products.
To participate in sexual exhibitionism.

exhibition.ety: From Old French exhibicion. Equivalent to exhibit + -ion.

ex.en: The exhibition will be open for another month.
ex.ja: 博覧会の会期はまだあと１カ月あります。

ex.en: You ought to have seen the exhibition.
ex.ja: 君はその展覧会を見るべきだったのに。

ex.en: The exhibition will be held next month.
ex.ja: その展覧会は来月開かれるでしょう。

note.ja: exhibit（展示する）+ -ion。ex（外へ）+ habere（持つ）。「外に持ち出して見せる」→「展覧会」。

en: The crime of stealing or otherwise illegally obtaining money by use of deception tactics.
Any act of deception carried out for the purpose of unfair, undeserved or unlawful gain.

fraud.ety: Inherited from Middle English fraude (recorded since 1345), from Old French fraude, a borrowing from Latin fraus (“deceit, injury, offence”).

ex.en: What he did is, in plain language, fraud.
ex.ja: 彼のしたことは手っ取り早く言えば詐欺だ。

ex.en: This paper has been treated so as to prevent fraud.
ex.ja: この用紙は、不正防止処置を施してあります。

ex.en: She is guilty of fraud.
ex.ja: 彼女は詐欺の罪を犯している。

note.ja: ラテン語 fraus（だまし）から。「詐欺」。

en: A ceremony to honor and remember a deceased person, often distinguished from a memorial service by the presence of the body of the deceased.

funeral.ety:
Borrowed from Middle French funerailles pl (“funeral rites”), from Medieval Latin fūnerālia (“funeral rites”), originally neuter plural of Late Latin fūnerālis (“having to do with a funeral”), from Latin fūnus (“funeral, death, corpse”), origin unknown, perhaps ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dʰew- (“to die”). Singular and plural used interchangeably in English until circa 1700. The adjective funereal is first attested 1725, by influence of Middle French funerail, from Latin funereus, from funus. First attested in 1437.
Displaced native Old English līcþeġnung (literally “dead body service

ex.en: I have to go to a funeral today.
ex.ja: 今日はお葬式に行かなきゃいけないの。

ex.en: It is traditional to wear black to a funeral.
ex.ja: 葬式には黒い服を着ていくのが習慣です。

ex.en: All his political enemies showed themselves at his funeral.
ex.ja: 彼の政敵すべてが彼の葬儀に現れた。

note.ja: ラテン語 funeralis（葬式の）から。funus（葬式）。

en: Belonging to, or proceeding from the original stock; native.
Not counterfeit, spurious, false, or adulterated.

ex.en: This is a writing style different from genuine English.
ex.ja: これは純正の英語とは違った文体だ。

ex.en: That football is made of genuine leather.
ex.ja: あのサッカーボールは本物の革でできている。

ex.en: Those present took it for genuine gold.
ex.ja: 出席者はそれを純金だと思った。

note.ja: ラテン語 genuinus（生まれつきの）から。「本物の」。gene、genus と同系とされる。

en: A sweet, viscous, gold-colored fluid produced from plant nectar by bees, and often consumed by humans.
A variety of this substance.
Involving or resembling honey.
Of a pale yellow to brownish-yellow color, like most types of honey.
To sweeten; to make agreeable.
To add honey to.

honey.ety:

ex.en: Honey, will you go shopping for me?
ex.ja: ねえあなた、私の代わりに買い物へ行ってくださる？

ex.en: Tom puts honey in his tea instead of sugar.
ex.ja: トムは、砂糖のかわりにハチミツを紅茶にいれます。

ex.en: There is some honey on the table.
ex.ja: 食卓には蜂蜜が置いてあります。

note.ja: 古英語 hunig から。「はちみつ」→ 甘いもののように「あなた（呼びかけ）」。

en: A rod bent into a curved shape, typically with one end free and the other end secured to a rope or other attachment.
A barbed metal hook used for fishing; a fishhook.
To attach a hook to.
To become attached, as by a hook.

hook.ety:
From Middle English hoke, from Old English hōc (“angle, point, hook”), from Proto-West Germanic *hōk, from Proto-Germanic *hōkaz, variant of *hakô (“hook”), probably ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kog-, *keg-, *keng- (“peg, hook, claw”).

Cognate with Scots huke, huik (“hook”), West Frisian and Dutch hoek (“hook, angle, corner”), Low German Hook, Huuk, German Hook (“small cluster of farms”), Faroese høkja (“crutch”), Icelandic hækja (“crutch”), Norn hek (“crutch”), Finnish kuokka (“hoe, mattock”). Related to hake.

ex.en: Let me off the hook this time, please.
ex.ja: 今回は見逃してください。

ex.en: Will you get me off the hook this time?
ex.ja: 今回は見逃してくれよ。

ex.en: A strange fish is on the hook.
ex.ja: 変な魚が針にかかっている。

note.ja: 古英語 hōc から。「かぎ」→「引っかける」→「夢中にさせる」。

en: One who hunts game for sport or for food; a huntsman or huntswoman.
A dog used in hunting; a hunting dog.

hunter.ety: From Middle English huntere, hunter, equivalent to hunt + -er. Compare Old English hunta (“hunter”).

ex.en: Man is the hunter, woman is his game.
ex.ja: 男は狩人で、女はその獲物である。

ex.en: The hunter shot at the bird.
ex.ja: ハンターは鳥をねらって撃った。

ex.en: The hunter went deep into the forest, never to return.
ex.ja: その猟師は森の中深く入り込み、二度と帰らなかった。

note.ja: hunt（狩る）+ -er。「狩猟者」。

en: A non-native person who comes to a country from another country to permanently settle there.
A plant or animal that establishes itself in an area where it previously did not exist.
Of or relating to immigrants or the act of immigrating.

immigrant.ety: From Latin immigrans, present active participle of immigrāre (“to migrate into”), from in- (“into”) + migrāre (“to migrate”).

ex.en: Many immigrants to Britain have come from Asia.
ex.ja: 英国への多くの移民はアジアからきている。

ex.en: That country has a lot of immigrants from Europe.
ex.ja: その国にはヨーロッパからの移民が多い。

ex.en: America is a land of immigrants.
ex.ja: アメリカは移民の国である。

note.ja: im（中へ）+ migr（移る）+ ant（人）。中へ移り住む人 →「（外国からの）移民」。emigrant（外へ移る人）と対。

An instance of the information or knowledge so furnished.

ex.ja: 私はあなたの指図どおりにそれをいたします。

ex.ja: 学生たちはこれらの指示を無視している。

ex.ja: 解答はすべて指示に従って書かねばならない。

note.ja: in（中に）+ struct（積む）+ ion。（知識を）中に積み上げること →「教えること・指示・説明書」。

en: Money or property bequeathed to someone in a will.
Something inherited from a predecessor or the past.
Left over from the past; old and no longer current.
Belonging to a class of boardgame where permanent changes are made to game elements such as the board, cards and rules over multiple play…

legacy.ety:
From Middle English legacie, from Old French legacie and Medieval Latin lēgātia, from Latin lēgātum. Compare legatee.
The boardgame sense was coined by game designer Rob Daviau in 2011 with the game Risk Legacy.

ex.en: The old bridge is a legacy of the Roman Empire.
ex.ja: その古い橋はローマ帝国の遺産だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 legatus（委任された）から。lex（法）の仲間。遺言で委ねられたもの →「遺産・遺物」。

en: The trunk of a dead tree, cleared of branches.
Any bulky piece as cut from the above, used as timber, fuel etc.
To cut trees into logs.
To cut down (trees).

log.ety:
From Middle English logge, logg (first recorded in Anglo-Latin as loggum), of uncertain origin, but probably from Old Norse lóg, lág (“felled tree, log”), derived from Old Norse liggja (“to lie”). If so, then cognate with Norwegian låg (“fallen tree”), Dutch loog (“wood, timber, lumber”).
Alternatively, directly from Norwegian låg (“fallen tree”), which could have been borrowed through the Norwegian timber trade. However the Old Norse/Middle Norwegian vowel is long while Middle English vowel is short.

ex.en: Tom was sitting on a log, playing guitar.
ex.ja: トムはギターを弾きながら、丸太に腰かけていた。

ex.en: Tom is sleeping like a log.
ex.ja: トム、爆睡してるよ。

ex.en: The writer is living in a log cabin.
ex.ja: その作家は丸太小屋に住んでいる。

note.ja: 中英語 logge（丸太）から。航海で丸太を流して船の速さを測り、その記録を log book に書いたことから「記録・ログ」。

en: Without any other reason etc.; only, just, and nothing more.

merely.ety: From Middle English mereli, equivalent to mere + -ly.

ex.en: It is merely a matter of form.
ex.ja: それは形式上の問題に過ぎない。

ex.en: He was merely sitting in the place.
ex.ja: 彼はその場所でただ座っていた。

ex.en: He said it merely as a joke.
ex.ja: 彼は単に冗談としてそれを言った。

note.ja: mere（単なる）+ -ly。ラテン語 merus（混じりけのない）。「混じりけなく」→「単に」。

en: Someone who watches over something; a person in charge of something or someone.
A device that detects and informs on the presence, quantity, etc., of something.
To watch over; to guard.

monitor.ety: From Latin monitor (“warner”), from perfect passive participle monitus (“warning”), from verb monere (“to warn, admonish, remind”). Warship sense is from USS Monitor, the first ship of this type.

ex.en: What's the reading on the blood pressure monitor?
ex.ja: 血圧計の数値は？

ex.en: I'm having trouble reading the letters on the monitor.
ex.ja: 私はモニターの文字を読む事が困難です。

ex.en: I use it as both a television and a monitor.
ex.ja: テレビとモニタを兼用してる。

note.ja: ラテン語 monitor（忠告する人）から。monere（警告する）。「見張る人」→「監視装置・画面」。monster、admonish と同系。

en: A person incarcerated in a prison, while on trial or serving a sentence.
Any person held against their will.

prisoner.ety: From Middle English prisoner, from Old French prisonier (compare Medieval Latin prisōnārius), equivalent to prison + -er.

ex.en: The prisoners were glad to be free again.
ex.ja: 囚人たちは釈放されて喜んだ。

ex.en: He ordered them to release the prisoners.
ex.ja: 彼は彼らに囚人を釈放するように命令した。

ex.en: The prisoners fought one another like so many mad people.
ex.ja: その囚人達はまるで狂人のように互いに争った。

note.ja: prison（刑務所）+ -er。「囚人・捕虜」。

en: The industry of publishing, including the production and distribution of books, magazines, web sites, newspapers, etc.
Something published; a publication.

ex.en: That publishing company is in the black.
ex.ja: あの出版社は黒字だ。

ex.en: He is in the publishing business.
ex.ja: 彼は出版の仕事に従事している。

ex.en: She has been with a publishing company for two years.
ex.ja: 彼女は出版社に２年勤めている。

note.ja: publish（出版する）+ -ing。「出版業」。

en: A number representing a comparison between two named things.
The relative magnitudes of two quantities (usually expressed as a quotient).
Indicates disagreement with a post the user disagrees with or dislikes.

ratio.ety: Borrowed from Latin ratiō. Doublet of ration and reason.

ex.en: This job is does not have a suitable profit ratio.
ex.ja: この仕事は割に合わない。

ex.en: The merger was implemented on a 50-50 ratio.
ex.ja: その合併は１対１で行われた。

note.ja: ラテン語 ratio（計算）から。計算された関係 →「比率」。reason（理由）、rate（割合）も同じ。

To feel sorry about (any thing).
Emotional pain on account of something done or experienced in the past, with a wish that it had been different; a looking back with dissa…
The amount of avoidable loss that results from choosing the wrong action.

ex.en: The time will come when you'll regret it.
ex.ja: それを後悔する時が来ますよ。

ex.ja: もっと勉強しなかったことを後悔している。

ex.ja: 今夜あなたに会えないのは、残念です。

en: To refuse to accept; to forswear.
To block a shot, especially if it sends the ball off the court.
Something that is rejected.
A rejected defective product in a production line.

reject.ety: From Late Middle English rejecten, from Latin reiectus, past participle of reicere (“to throw back”), from re- (“back”) + iacere (“to throw”). Displaced native Old English āweorpan (literally “to throw out”).

ex.ja: 会社は彼の転勤願いを却下した。

ex.ja: その客は私が見せたものを全部いやだといった。

ex.ja: その一行に加わりたいと言う彼女の申し出は拒否された。

ex.ja: ジョンに９時に電話することを私が忘れていたら教えてね。

ex.ja: これらの手紙を投函することを忘れていたら注意してくれませんか。

The opposite of something.
The act of going backwards; a reversal.

en: A course of action to be followed regularly; a standard procedure.

According to established procedure.
Regular; habitual.

ex.ja: 朝食前に新聞を読むのが私の日課です。

note.ja: フランス語 routine（決まった道筋）から。route（道）。「日課・決まった手順」。

A magical effect or influence induced by an incantation or formula.
To put under the influence of a spell; to affect by a spell; to bewitch; to fascinate; to charm.

en: Concise, brief, or presented in a condensed form; presenting information in such a form.
Performed speedily, without formal ceremony, and (especially) without regard to legality.
An abstract or a condensed presentation of the substance of a body of material.

en: An inheritance; property that may be inherited.
A tradition; a practice or set of values that is passed down from preceding generations through families or through institutional memory.

ex.ja: この建物は国民的遺産として保存すべきだ。

ex.en: We have a rich historical heritage.
ex.ja: 我々には豊かな歴史的遺産がある。

ex.en: I'm very proud of my heritage.
ex.ja: 私は、自分が先祖から受け継いだものにとても誇りを持っている。

note.ja: 古フランス語 heritage（相続財産）から。heriter（相続する）、ラテン語 heres（相続人）。heir、inherit と同じ。

en: In which voter initiatives can be brought to the ballot.
A beginning; a first move.
A new development; a fresh approach to something; a new way of dealing with a problem.

ex.ja: 彼は率先して計画を実行した。

en: A liquid made from plant, especially fruit.

ex.ja: この英作文はよくできすぎている。

ex.ja: 私は先生に英作文を直してもらった。

en: The act of preserving, guarding, or protecting; the keeping (of a thing) in a safe or entire state; preservation.
Wise use of natural resources.

conservation.ety: From Old French. By surface analysis, conserve + -ation.

ex.en: Forest conservation is an important issue all over the world.
ex.ja: 森林の保護は世界中の重要な問題だ。

ex.en: The organization plays a principal role in wildlife conservation.
ex.ja: その団体は野生動物の保護において、最も重要な役割を果たしている。

ex.en: This has been designated a conservation area.
ex.ja: この地域は保全地域に指定されています。

note.ja: conserve（保存する）+ -ation。con + servare（保つ）。「保護・保存」。preserve と同じ serv。

en: Belonging to, or inherent in, the constitution or structure of one's body or mind.
For the benefit of one's constitution or health.
A walk that is taken regularly for good health and wellbeing.
An act of defecation.

en: A measure of the mass of matter contained by a unit volume.
The ratio of one quantity, representing something of interest, to another quantity representing space, area, or extent in which the thing…

density.ety: Borrowed from Middle French densité or Latin densitas. Morphologically dense + -ity.

ex.ja: 日本は人口密度が高い国である。

ex.en: What's the country with the highest population density in the world?
ex.ja: 世界で一番人口が密集している国はどこですか？

ex.en: A recent survey revealed that the population density in the metropolis was decreasing.
ex.ja: 最近の調査は大都市の人口密度がていかしていることを示した。

note.ja: dense（密な）+ -ity。ラテン語 densus（濃い）。「密度」。condense と同じ。

en: The state of being difficult, or hard to do.
An obstacle that hinders achievement of a goal.

difficulty.ety: From Middle English difficulte, from Middle French and Anglo-Norman difficulte and their etymon Latin difficultas, from difficul, older form of difficilis (“hard to do, difficult”), from dis- + facilis (“easy”); see difficile and difficult. Equivalent to dis- + facile + -ty. Also analysable as difficult + -y, though the adjective is historically a backformation from the noun.

ex.en: I had no difficulty in finding his office.
ex.ja: 簡単に彼の事務所が見付かった。

ex.en: He had no difficulty in finding the place.
ex.ja: 彼は難なくその場所を見つけた。

ex.en: We can get over the problem without difficulty.
ex.ja: その問題は難なく克服できる。

note.ja: dif（否定）+ fic（する）+ ult + y。容易にできないこと →「困難」。

en: Relating to the basic, essential or fundamental part of something.
Very simple.
A supernatural being associated with the elements.

elementary.ety: From Middle English elementare, from Latin elementārius (“elementary”), from elementum (“one of the four elements of antiquity; fundamentals”) + -ārius (adjective-forming suffix). Cognate with French élémentaire. By surface analysis, element + -ary.

ex.en: There used to be an elementary school here.
ex.ja: ここにもとは小学校があった。

ex.en: My little brother goes to an elementary school.
ex.ja: 弟は小学校へ通っています。

ex.en: He is in fourth grade of elementary school.
ex.ja: 彼は小学４年生です。

note.ja: element（要素）+ -ary。「基本的な」→「初歩の」→ elementary school（小学校）。

The demonym of an Ancient Greek city.

en: A spending or consuming, often a disbursement of funds.
The elimination or consumption of something, sometimes with the notion of loss or damage to the thing eliminated.
To charge a cost against an expense account; to bill something to the company for which one works.

expense.ety: From Middle English expense, from Anglo-Norman expense and Old French espense, from Late Latin expēnsa, from Latin expendō. See expend. Doublet of speso.

ex.en: We must cut our expenses to save money.
ex.ja: 金をためるには出費を切りつめないと。

ex.en: You had better cut down your living expenses.
ex.ja: あなたは生活費を切り詰めた方がいいですよ。

ex.en: My living expense is rising year by year.
ex.ja: 私の生活費は年々上がっている。

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ pens（量る・支払う）+ e。量って支払い出すもの →「費用・出費」。

en: A group of vessels or vehicles, generally operating in a unified way or traveling together.
The vehicles commercially owned by a person, company or agency.
To pass over rapidly; to skim the surface of.
To hasten over; to cause to pass away lightly, or in mirth and joy.
Swift in motion; light and quick in going from place to place.
Light; superficially thin; not penetrating deep, as soil.

fleet.ety: From Middle English flete, flet (“fleet”), from Old English flēot (“ship”), likely related to Proto-West Germanic *flotōn, from Proto-Germanic *flutōną (“to float”).

ex.en: Art is long, time is fleeting.
ex.ja: 少年老い易く学成り難し。

ex.en: Our combined fleet broke through the enemy's defense zone.
ex.ja: わが連合艦隊は敵の防衛海域を突破した。

ex.en: Human life is fleeting.
ex.ja: 人の命は儚い。

note.ja: 古英語 flēot（船）から。float、flow と同系。「艦隊」。

en: Someone possessing extraordinary intelligence or skill; especially somebody who has demonstrated this by a creative or original work in s…
Extraordinary mental capacity.
Ingenious, brilliant, very clever, or original.

genius.ety: From Latin genius (“inborn nature; a tutelary deity of a person or place; wit, brilliance”), from gignō (“to beget, produce”), Old Latin genō, from the Proto-Indo-European root *ǵenh₁-. Doublet of genio. See also genus and genie.

ex.en: He is what we call a musical genius.
ex.ja: 彼はいわゆる音楽的天才である。

ex.en: It is believed that she is a genius.
ex.ja: 彼女は天才だと信じられている。

ex.en: In a word, he is a man of genius.
ex.ja: 一言で言えば彼は天才だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 genius（生まれつきの守護神）から。gen（生まれる）。生まれ持った才 →「天才・才能」。

en: To a great extent or degree.

greatly.ety: Inherited from Middle English gretly. By surface analysis, great + -ly.

ex.ja: 海で泳ぐことは私の一番の楽しみだ。

ex.en: The greater part of the money was spent.
ex.ja: その金の大部分が使われた。

ex.en: We conducted our investigation with the greatest care.
ex.ja: 私たちはきわめて慎重に調査を行なった。

note.ja: great + -ly。「大いに」。

An uncontrolled growth of harmful microorganisms in a host.

infection.ety: From Old French infection, from Late Latin īnfectiō. Equivalent to infect + -ion.

ex.ja: 中耳炎になったことはありますか？

ex.en: The spread of the infection is very dangerous.
ex.ja: 感染の広がりはとても危ないです。

ex.en: I have an ear infection.
ex.ja: 耳がかぶれています。

en: Of high value or worth.
Regarded with love or tenderness.
Someone (or something) who is loved; a darling.
Very; an intensifier.

precious.ety: Inherited from Middle English precious, borrowed from Old French precios (“valuable, costly, precious, beloved, also affected, finical”), from Latin pretiōsus (“of great value, costly, dear, precious”), from pretium (“value, price”); see price.

ex.en: Gold is more precious than any other metal.
ex.ja: 金は、あらゆる金属の中で最も貴重である。

ex.en: Health is the most precious thing we have.
ex.ja: 私たちにとって健康は一番大切なものです。

ex.en: Time is the most precious thing of all.
ex.ja: 時間は最も貴重なものだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 pretiosus（高価な）から。pretium（値段）。「貴重な」。price、appreciate と同じ。

en: The condition of being pregnant; an instance of this.
The period of time this condition prevails.

ex.en: I had an ectopic pregnancy two years ago.
ex.ja: ２年前に子宮外妊娠をしました。

ex.en: Let's do a pregnancy test.
ex.ja: 妊娠の検査をしましょう。

High-end; belonging to the market segment between mid-market and luxury.
A prize or award.
Something offered at a reduced price as an inducement to buy something else.

ex.en: Does this car use regular or premium?
ex.ja: この車って、レギュラー？ハイオク？

ex.en: You pay 10,000 yen a month as an insurance premium.
ex.ja: その保険の掛け金は１ヶ月１万円だ。

To ordain as a priest.

priest.ety:

In Nazi concentration camps, an inmate entrusted with minor supervisory duties and rewarded with perquisites.

ex.ja: 彼は会社で重要な地位を占めている。

ex.ja: その著名な心理学者は、見た目が私の叔父に似ている。

A trip during which people temporarily live together.

ex.en: This residential area is comfortable to live in.
ex.ja: この住宅地域は住み心地がよい。

ex.en: A factory is not suitable for a residential district.
ex.ja: 工場は住宅地域にはふさわしくない。

ex.en: Tom and Mary live in a quiet residential neighborhood.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーは閑静な住宅街に住んでいる。

note.ja: residence（住居）+ -ial。「住宅の」。resident と同じ。

en: Something of value given in return for an act.
A prize promised for a certain deed or catch
To give a reward to or for.
To be a recompense for.

reward.ety:
From Middle English reward, rewarde, from Old French reward (“reward”) (compare Old French regard, whence modern French regard, and also English regard through Middle French), from rewarder (“to reward”) (compare Old French reguarder), from re- + warder (“to guard, keep”) (compare Old French guarder); the Anglo-Norman forms are derived from Old Northern French variants of Old French, ultimately of Germanic (Frankish) origin. Compare regard, warden, guard. See more below.
Mostly displaced Old English mēd, whence Modern English meed. Displaced Old English lēan and edlēan.

ex.en: Not everyone is properly rewarded for his efforts.
ex.ja: 誰もが努力にふさわしい報酬を受けているわけではない。

ex.en: He wasn't given any reward for his service.
ex.ja: 彼は労働の報酬を何も貰わなかった。

ex.en: He was too proud to accept any reward.
ex.ja: 報酬を受け取るのを彼のプライドが許さなかった。

note.ja: 古フランス語 rewarder（見て報いる）から。re + warder（見守る）。「報酬・報いる」。regard、guard と同系。

en: A moon or other smaller body orbiting a larger one.
A man-made apparatus designed to be placed in orbit around a celestial body, generally to relay information, data, etc. to Earth.
To transmit by satellite.
To orbit, like a satellite

satellite.ety: From Middle French satellite, from Latin satelles (“attendant”). Ultimately perhaps of Etruscan origin.

ex.en: The moon is a satellite of the earth.
ex.ja: 月は地球の衛星である。

ex.en: The satellite is in orbit around the moon.
ex.ja: 衛星は月の周りの軌道に乗っている。

ex.en: Earth has one naturally occurring satellite, the Moon.
ex.ja: 地球は自然に発生した衛星を一つ有する。それは月だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 satelles（護衛）から。主人の周りを回る護衛 →「衛星」。

en: To cause (something) to move rapidly in opposite directions alternatingly.
To move (one's head) from side to side, especially to indicate refusal, reluctance, or disapproval.
The act of shaking or being shaken; tremulous or back-and-forth motion.
A twitch, a spasm, a tremor.

shake.ety:

English shake
From Middle English schaken, from Old English sċeacan, sċacan (“to shake”), from Proto-West Germanic *skakan, from Proto-Germanic *skakaną (“to shake, swing, escape”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)keg-, *(s)kek- (“to jump, move”).
Cognate with Scots schake, schack (“to shake”), West Frisian schaekje (“to shake”), Dutch schaken (“to elope, make clean, shake”), Low German schaken (“to move, shift, push, shake”) and schacken (“to shake, shock”),

ex.en: Our eyes should meet when we shake hands.
ex.ja: 握手をする時には、視線を合わすべきだ。

ex.en: Did you feel the earth shake last night?
ex.ja: 昨夜、地震を感じましたか。

ex.en: My faith in this country was never shaken.
ex.ja: この国に対する私の忠誠心は決して揺るがなかった。

note.ja: 古英語 sceacan から。「振る・揺れる」。milkshake は振って混ぜる飲み物。

en: Land adjoining a non-flowing body of water, such as an ocean, lake or pond.
Land, usually near a port.
Not followed by up: to provide (something) with support.
Usually followed by up: to reinforce (something at risk of failure).

shore.ety:
From Middle English schore, from Old English *sċora (attested as sċor- in placenames), from Proto-Germanic *skurô (“rugged rock, cliff, high rocky shore”). Possibly related to Old English sċieran (“to cut”), which survives today as English shear.
Cognate with Middle Dutch scorre (“land washed by the sea”), Middle Low German schor (“shore, coast, headland”), Middle High German schorre ("rocky crag, high rocky shore"; > German Schorre, Schorren (“towering rock, crag”)), and Limburgish sjaor (“riverbank”). Maybe connected with Norwegian Bokmål skjær.

ex.en: We walked along the shore of the lake.
ex.ja: 私たちは湖の岸に沿って歩いた。

ex.en: I found a beautiful shell on the shore.
ex.ja: 私は岸辺で美しい貝殻を見つけた。

ex.en: The ship stopped a little way off the shore.
ex.ja: その船は海岸を少し離れて停滞していた。

note.ja: 古英語 score から。shear（刈る）と同系とされ、陸の「切れ目」→「岸」。

en: Having a substance; actually existing.
Not imaginary; real; actual; true; veritable.
Anything having substance; an essential part.

substantial.ety: From Middle English substancial, substantiall, from Old French substanciel, substantiel and its etymon Latin substantiālis.

ex.en: It will require substantial time and financial resources.
ex.ja: それにはかなりの時間と費用がかかります。

ex.en: Thanks to the opportunity, we were able to avoid substantial effort.
ex.ja: この機会のおかげで私たちは大いに手間暇が省けた。

ex.en: He made a substantial contribution to economics.
ex.ja: 彼は経済学に相当な貢献をした。

note.ja: sub（下に）+ stan（立つ）+ tial。下にしっかり立っているもの（substance 実体）の →「かなりの・実質的な」。

en: The act of transmitting, e.g. data (signals) or electric power.
The fact of being transmitted.

transmission.ety: Borrowed from Latin transmissionem (accusative of transmissio), from transmittere.

ex.en: There might have been an error during transmission.
ex.ja: 受信異常があったのだと思います。

ex.en: 4-speed automatic transmission is available as an option.
ex.ja: オプションとして４速自動変速機も選べる。

ex.en: Can you drive a car with manual transmission?
ex.ja: マニュアルシフトで運転できますか。

note.ja: trans（向こうへ）+ miss（送る）+ ion。向こうへ送ること →「伝達・送信・変速装置」。

en: A machine or other device designed to catch (and sometimes kill) animals, either by holding them in a container, or by catching hold of p…
A trick or arrangement designed to catch someone in a more general sense; a snare.
To physically capture, to catch in a trap or traps, or something like a trap.
To ensnare; to take by stratagem; to entrap.

trap.ety:

Cognate with Dutch trap (“step, stair”), German Low German Trapp (“step, stair”). Akin also to West Frisian traap (“stepping, treading, stairway”), German Treppe (“step, stair”), Old English træppan (“to step, tread”). Connection to "step" is "that upon which one steps". French tr

ex.en: We set a trap to catch a fox.
ex.ja: 私たちは狐を捕まえるためにわなをしかけた。

ex.en: He set a trap to catch the animal.
ex.ja: 彼はその動物をとらえるためにわなをしかけた。

ex.en: She fell into a trap in her turn.
ex.ja: 彼女は今度は自分が罠にはまった。

note.ja: 古英語 træppe から。「わな」。
